name: PCA9685 16-channel PWM / servo driver
description: NXP 16-channel, 12-bit PWM controller on I2C (address 0x40-0x7F, default 0x40) with an internal 25 MHz oscillator; all channels share one frequency, 24-1526 Hz. Drives hobby servos at 50 Hz or LEDs; outputs sink up to 25 mA. Logic supply 3-5 V on this board; servos take separate power on V+. Sold as: Adafruit 16-Channel 12-bit PWM/Servo Driver - I2C interface - PCA9685 (#815), control header GND, OE, SCL, SDA, VCC, V+ (repeated on the opposite edge for chaining), 16 three-pin servo outputs (PWM, V+, GND), address jumpers A0-A5; also the many PCA9685 clone modules with the same header.
eli5: Lets your board control up to 16 servo motors or LEDs using just two wires, so the board doesn't have to make all those pulses itself.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground for logic and servos, must be connected

pins.name: OE
pins.description: Output enable, active low: pulled low on the board (outputs on); drive high to disable all outputs

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kOhm pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kOhm pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Logic supply for the PCA9685, 3-5 V; match your microcontroller (3.3 V for ESP32/Pico) since it also feeds the I2C pull-ups

pins.name: V+
pins.description: Servo power in, 5-6 V from a separate supply (not used by the chip); leave unconnected if not driving servos. Never connect to VCC or a 3.3 V pin

supplierQuery: PCA9685 16 channel PWM servo driver board I2C
buildNotes: Power the servos from a separate 5-6 V supply on V+ (or the screw terminal), sharing GND with the microcontroller. Never power servos from the 3.3 V pin.
VCC is the chip's logic supply and feeds the SDA/SCL pull-ups: use 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico.
The chip powers up asleep (MODE1 = 0x11). PRE_SCALE (0xFE) can only be written while SLEEP is set; prescale = round(25 MHz / (4096 x f)) - 1, so 121 for 50 Hz.
After clearing SLEEP wait 500 us for the oscillator before touching the PWM registers; set MODE1 AI (bit 5) to write the four LEDn bytes in one go.
Channel n uses LEDn_ON_L/H, LEDn_OFF_L/H at 0x06 + 4n (12-bit counts out of 4096); bit 4 of OFF_H = fully off, bit 4 of ON_H = fully on.
Address 0x40 by default; bridge A0-A5 solder jumpers for 0x41-0x7F to chain up to 62 boards.

driver.code:
# PCA9685 16-channel 12-bit PWM / servo driver (NXP PCA9685), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the NXP PCA9685 datasheet Rev. 4: MODE1 0x00, MODE2 0x01, LEDn_ON_L/H, LEDn_OFF_L/H at
# 0x06 + 4*n, ALL_LED at 0xFA, PRE_SCALE 0xFE (writable only while SLEEP=1),
# prescale = round(osc / (4096 * f)) - 1, clamped to 3..255; oscillator needs 500 us after wake.
import time

_MODE1 = 0x00
_MODE2 = 0x01
_LED0 = 0x06
_ALL_LED = 0xFA
_PRESCALE = 0xFE
_RESTART = 0x80
_AI = 0x20
_SLEEP = 0x10
_ALLCALL = 0x01
_OUTDRV = 0x04
_FULL = 0x10  # bit 4 of LEDn_ON_H (full on) / LEDn_OFF_H (full off)


class PCA9685:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x40, freq=50, osc=25000000):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.osc = osc  # internal oscillator, 25 MHz typical (real chips vary by a few %)
        self._freq = freq
        self._w(_MODE2, _OUTDRV)  # totem-pole outputs (POR default; needed by the Adafruit board)
        self._w(_ALL_LED + 2, 0)  # ALL_LED_OFF_L
        self._w(_ALL_LED + 3, _FULL)  # ALL_LED_OFF_H: every channel fully off
        self._w(_MODE1, _AI | _ALLCALL)  # wake, register auto-increment on
        time.sleep_us(500)  # oscillator start-up, datasheet MODE1 note [2]
        self.freq(freq)

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val & 0xFF]))

    def _r(self, reg):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 1)[0]

    def freq(self, hz=None):
        """Set (or return) the PWM frequency, 24..1526 Hz, shared by all 16 channels."""
        if hz is None:
            return self.osc / (4096 * (self._r(_PRESCALE) + 1))
        pre = int(self.osc / (4096 * hz) + 0.5) - 1
        pre = max(3, min(255, pre))
        old = self._r(_MODE1) & ~_RESTART & 0xFF
        self._w(_MODE1, old | _SLEEP)  # PRE_SCALE can only be written while asleep
        self._w(_PRESCALE, pre)
        self._w(_MODE1, (old & ~_SLEEP) | _AI)
        time.sleep_us(500)
        if self._r(_MODE1) & _RESTART:  # restart channels that were running (section 7.3.1.1)
            self._w(_MODE1, (old & ~_SLEEP) | _AI | _RESTART)
        self._freq = hz
        return pre

    def prescale(self):
        return self._r(_PRESCALE)

    def pwm(self, ch, on, off):
        """Raw 12-bit counts: output goes high at count `on` and low at count `off` (0..4095)."""
        if not 0 <= ch <= 15:
            raise ValueError('channel 0..15')
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _LED0 + 4 * ch,
                             bytes([on & 0xFF, (on >> 8) & 0x0F, off & 0xFF, (off >> 8) & 0x0F]))

    def duty(self, ch, value):
        """Duty cycle as 0..4095; 0 = fully off, 4095 = fully on."""
        if value <= 0:
            self.off(ch)
        elif value >= 4095:
            self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _LED0 + 4 * ch, bytes([0, _FULL, 0, 0]))
        else:
            self.pwm(ch, 0, value)

    def off(self, ch):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _LED0 + 4 * ch, bytes([0, 0, 0, _FULL]))

    def pulse_us(self, ch, us):
        """High pulse of `us` microseconds each period (servos: about 500..2500 us at 50 Hz)."""
        counts = int(us * self._freq * 4096 / 1000000 + 0.5)
        self.duty(ch, counts)
        return counts

    def servo(self, ch, angle, min_us=500, max_us=2500):
        """Move a hobby servo to 0..180 degrees. Check your servo's pulse range before going to the ends."""
        angle = max(0, min(180, angle))
        return self.pulse_us(ch, min_us + (max_us - min_us) * angle / 180)

    def all_off(self):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _ALL_LED, bytes([0, 0, 0, _FULL]))

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from pca9685 import PCA9685

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
pwm = PCA9685(i2c, freq=50)  # 50 Hz for hobby servos
counts = pwm.pulse_us(0, 1500)  # servo on channel 0 to centre
pwm.off(1)  # channel 1 fully off
print('prescale=%d ch0=%d' % (pwm.prescale(), counts))
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
